Palestinian human rights defender, farmer and veteran grassroots organiser Ghassan Najjar has been put into administrative detention for four months [File: Al Jazeera]By Daniel Khalili-TariPublished On 16 Nov 202616 Nov 2026
An Israeli military court has upheld a four–month administrative detention order against Palestinian land activist and farmer Ghassan Najjar.
Najjar appeared at Ofer Military Court on Monday. He was arrested during a pre–dawn raid on Burin village, south of Nablus, in the occupied West Bank on October 27, and has been held in administrative detention since.

The Israeli authorities have not given a reason for Najjar’s arrest, as administrative detention allows them. The Palestinian human rights defender, farmer and veteran grassroots organiser has a long history of arrest, having spent nearly a decade in Israeli prisons, much of it under administrative detention. He has been subjected to a travel ban since 2011.
The Institute for Middle East Understanding (IMEU) told Al Jazeera that Najjar was arrested because he intended to harvest olives on his land and planned to help other Palestinian farmers do the same. Israel’s security agency Shin Bet reportedly warned Najjar, cofounder of Burin’s Land and Farming Agricultural Cooperative, that he would be arrested if he did not stop organising with grassroots groups and Western activists.

Vehicles move beneath a giant billboard depicting killed members of the Kataib Hezbollah paramilitary group who were killed in an airstrike in al-Qaim, in Baghdad's eastern Sadr City suburb on September 21, 2026. [File: AFP]By Al Jazeera Staff, Anadolu and ReutersPublished On 16 Nov 202616 Nov 2026
Iraq has ordered its armed forces to move into a stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah group, amid an investigation into suspected oil smuggling.
Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has ordered the military to enter the town of Jurf al-Nasr, government spokesman Haidar al-Aboudi said on Monday, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA). The Iraqi leader has also set a deadline for the armed faction, which has been implicated in the oil probe, to leave the area.

Women sit on a bench overlooking cargo ships anchored in the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas, Iran, Friday, November 13, 2026 [Amirhosein Khorgooi/ISNA via AP]By Maziar MotamediPublished On 16 Nov 202616 Nov 2026
Tehran, Iran – Iran is heading into winter with warnings of natural gas shortages, as damage from strikes by the United States and Israel deepens an energy imbalance that has plagued the resource-rich country for years.
Iran holds the second-largest proven natural gas reserves in the world, only behind Russia, but its government last week forecast a peak-demand deficit of about 430 million cubic metres per day for winter that could impact both households and industries.

The country’s ageing energy infrastructure has long suffered from underinvestment and international sanctions that have restricted finances and equipment. Authorities say that inefficient consumption and limited storage capacity are also to blame, in addition to the damage from the ongoing war.
Saeed Tavakoli, head of the National Iranian Gas Company, told local media last week that 26 projectiles struck six refineries on March 18, knocking out 28 percent of Iran’s gas production capacity in the immediate aftermath of the strikes.
According to the government, about 100 million cubic metres per day of processing capacity has since been restored, but fully bringing back the additional 130 million cubic metres lost in the US and Israeli attacks could extend into 2028.

President of the French Football Federation (FFF) Philippe Diallo said in September that the FFF was withdrawing its backing for FIFA's current president, Gianni Infantino, in the upcoming election [Charly Tribbaleau/AFP]By AFPPublished On 16 Nov 202616 Nov 2026
European football’s governing body UEFA has given its “unanimous” backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election.
UEFA invited Diallo to “stand as a candidate in the FIFA presidential election in March 2027”, the continental body said in a statement on Monday, adding that European national associations had “unanimously pledged their full support”.
The deadline for rival candidates to declare themselves is Wednesday, November 18.
The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA), which boasts 55 member associations, said Diallo “has accepted the invitation to stand” and that his candidature is set to be confirmed at a meeting of the French Football Federation (FFF) on Tuesday.
Diallo, the 63-year-old son of a Senegalese boxing champion, has been president of the FFF since January 2023.
He was initially appointed to the post on an interim basis when previous chief Noel Le Graet was forced to stand down following a series of controversies.
Diallo, from Saint-Nazaire on France’s Atlantic coast, was then elected to the role by a large majority in June of that year, before being re-elected in December 2024 for a new four-year term.
UEFA’s months-long Infantino opposition
Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, UEFA has led the opposition to Infantino since his announcement in late July of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
